title: Beware of Hidden Risks in Medical Director Jobs
content:
Wellness centers, medical spas, and IV clinics are different; the practice needs a physician’s medical license in order to practice.

“The medical director’s license is what gives that practice authority to treat patients. The doctor may have no idea that it’s their license that allows this business to basically practice medicine. So…they are ultimately responsible for anything that goes wrong,” said Byrd. [...] That’s what happened to an anesthesiologist in Texas who became medical director of a medical spa offering intravenous (IV) infusions. In 2023, a 47-year-old patient died after the unlicensed medical spa owner gave an IV infusion treatment. Supervising medical director Michael P. Gallagher, MD, was about 100 miles away at the time. The infusion contained elements known to be fatal if infused too quickly. [...] Gallagher was charged with criminally negligent homicide, failure to supervise, and alleged delivery of a dangerous drug. The spa owner was also charged. Both pleaded not guilty.

In September 2026, the Texas Medical Board temporarily restricted Gallagher’s medical license. Pretrial hearings will take place later this month.

The case led to the creation of House Bill 3749, known as Jenifer’s CQ Law, which regulates elective intravenous IV therapy.
